topic: What happens to your body when a fighter jet pulls nine G?
title: Pulling Nine G
idea: Hard G drains the blood from your head, your sight shuts down in stages, and pilots squeeze it back up.
hook: You pull a hard turn in a fighter jet.

beats.line: At nine G, your head weighs nine times as much.
beats.see: G meter in the cockpit snaps to 9; the pilot's head sinks into the seat as a weight tag reads x9. Hits on 'nine' (second).

beats.line: The blood drains out of your head.
beats.see: Cutaway body: red blood level slides down from the head into the torso and legs like a falling thermometer. Hits on 'drains'.

beats.line: First the colors fade and the edges go gray.
beats.see: The whole frame loses color, then gray creeps in from the screen edges, the side of the cockpit vanishes. Hits on 'gray'.

beats.line: Then everything goes black, but you're still awake.
beats.see: Screen goes fully black; only the pilot's eyes stay open as two white cutouts blinking in the dark. Hits on 'black', eyes on 'awake'.

beats.line: Then the lights go out. Guess how long for.
beats.see: Eyes close, head drops forward; a big guess counter appears with '? SECONDS' and a ticking dial. Hits on 'out', counter on 'Guess'.

beats.line: About twelve seconds out cold. Then roughly fifteen more, confused.
beats.see: Counter spins to 12 with a stamp OUT COLD, then a second counter runs to 15 labeled CONFUSED while the pilot's eyes swirl. Hits on 'twelve' and 'fifteen'.

beats.line: Back to the start of the turn. Pilots fight back.
beats.see: Tape rewinds: color floods back, blood level rises; the pilot grips the stick and sets jaw. Rewind on 'Back', grip on 'fight'.

beats.line: One. Squeeze your legs and stomach hard.
beats.see: Step card 1 SQUEEZE; legs and belly tense and glow, blood level nudges up toward the head. Hits on 'Squeeze'.

beats.line: Two. Breathe in short, forced bursts.
beats.see: Step card 2 SHORT BREATHS; three quick puff clouds pop from the mask in rhythm. Hits on 'short' and 'bursts'.

beats.line: Three. Your G suit squeezes your legs tight.
beats.see: Step card 3 G SUIT; the trousers inflate like a balloon around the legs and the blood level holds at the head. Hits on 'squeezes'.

end.line: Pull the turn again, and this time keep the lights on.
end.see: Jet banks into the same turn as the hook; the frame stays in full color, pilot gives a thumbs up. Turn on 'Pull', color holds on 'lights'.

description: Pull nine G in a fighter jet and your sight shuts down in stages. Guess how long you black out.

facts.claim: At nine G everything weighs nine times as much, including your head.
facts.source: Basic physics, as listed in FACTS-batch-035-046.md (041)

facts.claim: High positive G pulls blood away from the head and the brain runs short of oxygen.
With slow onset the order is gray-out (loss of colour and side vision), black-out (no vision but still awake), then loss of consciousness (G-LOC).
G-LOC: about 12 seconds fully unconscious, then roughly 15 more seconds confused.
facts.source: Whinnery & Whinnery 1990, 501 centrifuge episodes (as listed in FACTS-batch-035-046.md, OK-number)

facts.claim: Pilots fight it with the anti-G straining manoeuvre (tense legs and abdomen, short forced breaths) and a G-suit that squeezes the legs.

notes: Stage order (gray, black, out) is the slow-onset order; with very fast onset there is no warning, which the script does not claim either way. 'Then the lights go out' = G-LOC. 'About twelve seconds' is the OK-number; 'roughly fifteen more' is from the same study. Did not use the 4 or 5 G threshold (snippet only). 'G suit' written without hyphen because of the no-dash rule. Big number: about twelve seconds.
